summary: The note profiles local inventors who are building smart-city technologies as urban populations grow. It covers projects in traffic optimization, pollution sensing, micro-mobility, breathing building materials, adaptive street lighting, mesh networking, civic engagement, solar tiles and subway aeroponic gardens, launched between September 2023 and April 2024. It argues these technologies make cities more efficient, sustainable and human.
one_line: Local inventors launched smart-city projects from September 2023 to April 2024, spanning mobility, materials, lighting, connectivity, civic apps, solar energy and urban farming.
key_facts: Over 55% of the world's population lives in urban areas, a figure expected to reach 68% by 2050.
James Ngai's startup GreenFlow introduced a traffic optimization system that uses AI to reduce congestion.
Priya Varma is launching a network of mobile pollution sensors.
Alejandro Gomez debuted eSkootr, a fleet of electric scooters placed across the city, in October 2023; users scan, ride and pay via an app, and smart-docking stations keep the scooters charged.

Tori Zinberg introduced BreathBlock in November 2023, a 'breathing' building material that responds to temperature and humidity to ventilate structures naturally; it is already used in several smart greenhouses around the city.
Danny Chui, known as 'Sensor Dan', rolled out SmartLightz in December 2023, adaptive street lamps with sensors for air quality, noise and pedestrian traffic that dim when no one is around.
Sandra Yi spearheaded CityMesh, the city's first large-scale mesh network, which came online in January 2024 and keeps internet access working during outages, congestion and emergencies.
Nathan Roche developed the CitySpeak app in February 2024, letting residents raise issues from potholes to policy proposals directly to officials.
Sofia Chang unveiled SunTiles in March 2024, solar tiles that integrate photovoltaic technology into almost any structure without compromising design.
Maggie Liu introduced AeroGardens in April 2024, vertical aeroponic gardens in subway stations where commuters can pick up fresh produce.
eSkootr is still in its nascent stage but has been followed by a noticeable decline in local traffic jams.
The note names IoT devices, AI and big data analytics as key elements of the Smart City.
